compile_track.description: Drop indent=2 from the cache JSON serialization (switch to compact separators), KEEPING sort_keys=True for deterministic output.
compile_track.mechanism: VERIFIED at line 7110: payload = json.dumps(serialized, indent=2, sort_keys=True). The cache is consumed programmatically only; indent=2 inflates file size and serialization time. Compact separators=(',',':') preserve all data and determinism (sort_keys stays). In-memory state and cache semantics identical.
compile_track.expected_effect: 5-15% faster cache saves on large caches; smaller cache files. No numerics change.
compile_track.synth_note: Verified locus; MUST retain sort_keys=True (determinism). Cheapest+safest compile win — bank first.

compile_track.description: In the per-trial timer closure, hoist _hash_sources(sources) to compute once per sweep and reuse on the common path where variant_sources==sources; only recompute for the poly/synth variant branch.
compile_track.mechanism: VERIFIED line 14832: variant_sources = list(sources) is taken unconditionally then replaced only in the poly/synth branch (which is OFF by default per the inline comment). The build_sig hash of sources is redundant per-trial when sources are unchanged. Hashing the same file set once and reusing is hash-value-identical, so cache keys are unchanged.
compile_track.expected_effect: 10-20% reduction in per-variant hash I/O during sweeps with thousands of trials (esp. poly/synth OFF). No cache-semantics change.
compile_track.synth_note: MERGED with variant-sources-list-copy-elision (same locus 14832, the list-copy is the cheaper half of this same hoist). High-value: hot per-trial path.

compile_track.description: Add a module-level per-arch cache for _version_gated_flags_for_hash(arch) / the nvcc version probe, so the deterministic result is computed once per process instead of re-derived in build_aot, the timer closure, and _device_cflags.
compile_track.mechanism: _version_gated_flags_for_hash(arch) is deterministic per arch (it probes nvcc once and maps to flags). It is invoked from at least 3 sites; in JIT sweeps the timer closure path runs thousands of times for the same arch. A lazy {arch->flags} dict eliminates redundant probes/derivation. Detected version and emitted flags are byte-identical, so no kernel codegen changes.
compile_track.expected_effect: 5-10% faster JIT sweeps (removes ~1000 redundant probe/derivation lookups); AOT sees 1-2 calls avoided.
compile_track.synth_note: MERGED 3 near-duplicates: version-gated-flags-cache + register-usage-level-early-probe + flag-probe-cache-warmup all reduce to 'cache the deterministic per-arch nvcc-version/flags result once'. Keep this best-described one.

compile_track.description: Order the prefilter rule evaluation cheapest/most-discriminating-first (e.g. dimension-bound checks like warps_per_block<=32 before cluster_volume*math) so configs that fail an early cheap rule skip the expensive rule evals. Same cartesian product, same survivors, same per-rule results — only short-circuit order changes.
compile_track.mechanism: VERIFIED compile_feasibility_check builds a closure of rules; reordering the rule list so high-rejection cheap rules run first short-circuits ~90% of candidates before the expensive checks. Survivors are bit-identical because rule predicates and the AND-composition are unchanged.
compile_track.expected_effect: 20-30% faster prefilter on exhaustive/billion-config sweeps; negligible on Bayesian (per-trial capped).
compile_track.synth_note: MERGED prefilter-early-exit-cartesian + prefilter-rule-ordering + feature-macro-dedup-and-order's ordering idea. The static cheap-first ordering (this one) is safe and needs no profiling pass; prefilter-rule-ordering's profile-driven reorder is the riskier variant folded in but de-scoped to the static form.

compile_track.description: Replace the list + del-slice rolling window for measured timings with collections.deque(maxlen=2000) so append+discard is O(1) instead of O(n) once the window fills.
compile_track.mechanism: VERIFIED lines 15752-15755: _meas.append(tms_f); if len>2000: del _meas[:len-2000]. deque(maxlen=2000) auto-discards in O(1). Iteration order is identical to the list, so the multi-fidelity quantile estimate is bit-identical and the cost-model rejection is unchanged.
compile_track.expected_effect: O(n)->O(1) window maintenance after cold-start; eliminates ~500k list-slice ops on 1000+ trial sweeps. Micro (0.1-1%) but in the hot timer path.
compile_track.synth_note: Verified locus. Self-contained, hot-path, bit-identical quantile — safe early win.

compile_track.locus: _multi_fidelity_prune_decision (lines 5802-5858), specifically 5834-5846 (finite-list build + sort) and the len(finite)<8 check
compile_track.description: Move the len(finite)<8 early-return BEFORE the finite-list filter + sort so short/cold-start windows skip the wasted comprehension and O(n log n) sort.
compile_track.mechanism: The function currently builds and sorts the finite list, then returns False when <8 samples (never using the sorted list). Reordering the length guard ahead of the filter/sort eliminates wasted work; the <8 semantics are unchanged.
compile_track.expected_effect: Eliminates list-build+sort on every multi-fidelity check with <8 samples (common at cold-start / short sweeps). 0.5-2% on short sweeps.
compile_track.synth_note: Pure reordering, identical decision. Pairs naturally with measured-ms-window-algo (same pruning machinery).

compile_track.description: Pre-compute the needed dim value lists (vec/unroll/ns) once from dim_by_name at the top of featurize_config instead of calling the _values_of dict-lookup helper ~6 times per config.
compile_track.mechanism: dim_by_name is built once (line 5201); the 6 repeated _values_of(name) dict.get lookups per feature vector are redundant. Hoisting the 3 distinct lookups to locals yields a bit-identical feature vector (cost-model input unchanged).
compile_track.expected_effect: 1-3% when cost model is active (featurize is called ~15-20x/trial); negligible when CM disabled.
compile_track.synth_note: MERGED featurize-config-dim-index + dim-by-name-cache-featurize + config-key-dead-dims-cache (all 'hoist a per-call lookup-table build out of a hot featurize/key function'). Keep the in-call hoist (this one); the lru_cache variant is unneeded complexity.

compile_track.description: Hoist the loop-invariant dim_names / dim_value_sets construction (lines 6327-6330) out of the seed_trials loop to before it; leave per-trial validation unchanged.
compile_track.mechanism: dim_names and dim_value_sets do not depend on the seed-trial iterate, so building them per-iteration is redundant. Moving them above the loop is a straight refactor with identical validation behavior.
compile_track.expected_effect: 1-5% when seed trials are used (saves 150-750 redundant list/dict builds); negligible when 0 seed trials (common).
compile_track.synth_note: Verified pattern; trivially safe loop-invariant hoist. Only bites when seed_trials set.

compile_track.description: Cache the recent-window tail-slice used for the EI computation and invalidate it only when observe() extends the window, instead of re-slicing on every should_stop() poll.
compile_track.mechanism: _improvement_window is append-only (in observe()); should_stop() re-slices [-patience:] every poll even when no new observation arrived. Caching the slice and dirtying it in observe() yields identical EI inputs.
compile_track.expected_effect: 1-3% on long sweeps (eliminates 900+ redundant slices when should_stop polls every trial with patience 50-100).
compile_track.synth_note: Self-contained; EI logic byte-identical. Slightly lower confidence than the pure hoists so ordered after them.

compile_track.description: Use numpy.percentile for the multi-fidelity quantile when numpy is already imported (featurize_config imports it unconditionally nearby), keeping the existing pure-Python fallback if numpy import fails.
compile_track.mechanism: The manual Python linear-interpolation quantile is ~5-10x slower than np.percentile on the trimmed window. numpy is already loaded on this path. RISK NOTE: np.percentile default linear interpolation must match the existing manual formula exactly; this only affects the PRUNE decision (not kernel numerics), so a tiny quantile delta cannot break fp64 parity — but it CAN change which configs get pruned, altering the search trajectory. Confirm the interpolation method matches before keeping.
compile_track.expected_effect: 1-3% when cost-model+multi-fidelity enabled; saves ~0.1-0.5ms per multi-fidelity check.
compile_track.synth_note: Search-trajectory-affecting (not output-affecting). Ordered last in compile_track: must byte-verify np.percentile matches the manual interpolation, else search results drift vs the recorded baseline.

kernel_track.locus: dec_tc_launcher_scratch() lines 55-71; mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc() lines 114-121 (cudaGetDevice + cudaDeviceGetAttribute on every call); vit launcher ~80-86; mamba launcher ~104-113
kernel_track.description: Cache n_sms (and the device id) in the per-device launcher scratch struct, computed once per device, instead of calling cudaGetDevice + cudaDeviceGetAttribute(MultiProcessorCount) on every launcher invocation in the training loop.
kernel_track.mechanism: VERIFIED lines 114-121: both CUDA API calls run every step. n_sms is a fixed per-device property; the launcher already maintains a per-device DecTcLauncherScratch (dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev,need)). Storing n_sms there (set on first touch of a device) removes 2 host-side CUDA calls per step. Kernel launch params, grid barrier, and all device-side numerics are byte-identical — this is host-side only and CANNOT affect fp64 parity.
kernel_track.expected_effect: ~1-2% reduction in host launcher overhead per optimizer step on single-GPU training; affects decoder/vit/mamba equally.
kernel_track.synth_note: MERGED launcher_cond_alloc + sg2_launcher_cond_alloc (identical hoist, applied to base + SG2 entry points). Host-side, parity-trivial (kernel unchanged), highest-confidence kernel-track win — bank first. Still runs the parity gate per protocol but it is a formality here.

kernel_track.locus: mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc() lines 120-121 (if (ncta_cap>0 && ncta_cap<nCTA) nCTA=ncta_cap); vit ~85-86; mamba ~112-113
kernel_track.description: Replace the short-circuit conditional nCTA cap with a branchless min: nCTA = (ncta_cap>0) ? min(n_sms, ncta_cap) : n_sms. Host-side cold-path tidy; identical resulting nCTA.
kernel_track.mechanism: VERIFIED line 120-121. The resulting nCTA value is identical for all inputs (ncta_cap<=0 -> n_sms; else min). Branchless form is purely a host-side codegen tidy. nCTA feeds the grid dim only; device numerics unchanged, parity-trivial.
kernel_track.expected_effect: Negligible (~0.01-0.05% host); consistency/clarity. Bundle with launcher_cond_alloc since same files/lines.
kernel_track.synth_note: Co-located with launcher_cond_alloc (same 3 launcher files, adjacent lines). Apply together to amortize the build+gate cost. Value is mostly bundling, not standalone.

kernel_track.description: Ensure the LBO/SBO descriptor field computations fold at compile time when MN is a template parameter (mark the lbo/sbo locals constexpr) so no runtime multiply/shift is emitted per descriptor build in the consumer k-loop.
kernel_track.mechanism: VERIFIED lines 276-277/285-286: lbo = (uint32_t)MN*16u, sbo=128u — already const uint32_t with template-constant MN, so a good compiler already folds these. Making them explicitly constexpr (and confirming make_smem_desc's >>4 folds) is a belt-and-suspenders codegen hint. These functions ARE on the production path (called by all 3 model_stage_*_tc.cuh). Descriptor bits are bit-identical, so wgmma inputs and fp64 parity are unchanged.
kernel_track.expected_effect: 0-2% in the descriptor-gen arithmetic of long-K tiles; likely already folded, so realistically ~0 but cannot regress.
kernel_track.synth_note: MERGED descriptor_base_offset_constexpr + smem_desc_immediate_encoding (both 'fold/cheapen the make_*desc bit-assembly'). Production-real (unlike the tile_pipeline turnkey candidates). Likely a no-op since already const-foldable; keep only if 3-seed timing shows a real delta. Parity gate required because it touches the GEMM descriptor path.

kernel_track.locus: dectc_wbf_convert (lines 327-352): bf16 weight-cache conversion, runtime tr=i>=kWbfTotalElems split + per-iter modulo/division for the transposed section
kernel_track.description: Split the single conversion loop (with the per-iteration boolean tr and the off%nout / off/nout for the transposed section) into two compile-time-bounded loops (straight section then transposed section) so the per-iteration branch and modulo/division are removed.
kernel_track.mechanism: VERIFIED the section boundary kWbfTotalElems is a compile-time constant, so the loop can be statically partitioned into [0,kWbfTotalElems) and [kWbfTotalElems,kWbfCacheElems) with dedicated index arithmetic. The bf16 values written to the cache are bit-identical (same source elements to same destinations), so parity holds. Runs in P0 (cache conversion, ~1% of wall, overlaps other CTA work).
kernel_track.synth_note: Real production code (decoder weight prestage). Low ceiling (P0 overlaps), low confidence — ordered near the end. Parity gate required (touches the bf16 weight cache feeding the GEMM).

kernel_track.locus: vittc_forward_tile, lines 850-856 (head-logits inner dot over vit::kD=128, currently #pragma unroll 4)
kernel_track.description: Raise the head-logits inner k-loop unroll from 4 to 8 to expose more independent fp32 FMA chains, without changing accumulation order or data types.
kernel_track.mechanism: A single float accumulator over 128 elements with a single bf16 load per step; unroll 8 keeps the SAME left-to-right accumulation order (no reassociation), so the fp32 sum is bit-identical and parity holds. More in-flight FMAs improve ILP on the 256-thread CTA. RISK: unroll factor changes can nudge ptxas register allocation; the gate's 3-seed timing + parity catches any regression.
kernel_track.expected_effect: 1-3% on the head fwd sub-phase; ~1-2% of total step at most.
kernel_track.synth_note: Pure unroll-factor bump, same accumulation order => parity-safe by construction. Highest-confidence among the ILP-unroll candidates. Verify ptxas doesn't spill (3-seed timing gate).

kernel_track.locus: vittc_attn_bwd_tile, lines 913-931 (dscores inner loop over kSeq=17, currently not unrolled)
kernel_track.description: Add #pragma unroll on the compile-time-bounded kSeq=17 dscores loop in attention backward to expose the 17 independent multiply-accumulate chains; ascending-kj order preserved.
kernel_track.mechanism: kSeq=17 is compile-time fixed; full unroll adds ~34 instructions with no register explosion and keeps the SAME ascending-kj order, so dscores accumulation is bit-identical. ILP-only change.
kernel_track.expected_effect: 0.5-1% on attention bwd (~5-8% of P2); ~0.025-0.04% overall.
kernel_track.synth_note: Same class as vit-head-logits-unroll (order-preserving unroll on a fixed bound). Low ceiling but parity-safe. Gate confirms no spill.

kernel_track.description: Relax the conservative #pragma unroll 1 on the HBM->smem staging loop (per call site) to allow ILP unroll of the cp.async/STS issue in the fwd/dX/dW projection staging, where the staging overlaps wgmma and is not the critical path.
kernel_track.mechanism: The staging loop only writes smem; the bytes landed and their offsets are unchanged by unrolling, so the GEMM operand tile is bit-identical and parity holds (determinism unchanged). Relaxing unroll 1 lets ptxas issue multiple STS/cp.async per iteration. RISK: must NOT change the cp.async double-buffer WAR choreography — apply only to the staging issue loop body, not the ring barrier sequence. Keep the generic template at unroll 1 and relax per-call-site.
kernel_track.expected_effect: 0.5-1% on projection GEMMs (projected GEMMs are a small wall fraction; diminishing returns).
kernel_track.synth_note: Production-real (mamba staging). Lower confidence: unroll on a staging loop can raise register pressure in the producer warpgroup (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40 budget). Ordered after the order-preserving fp32 unrolls. Parity gate mandatory (GEMM operand path).

kernel_track.locus: sm.red 256-float reduction slot used by GrokAdamW P2.5 (lines ~751-759), LookSAM P2.4 norm (~748-768), Prodigy P2.6 (~863-890); analogous fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh 752-759
kernel_track.description: Pad the sm.red reduction slot to 257 floats so the power-of-2 tree reduction's stride-128 accesses no longer collide on the 64-bank H100 (stride 128 floats = 512B = 2x32-way conflict). Reduction order/values unchanged; only a 4-byte slack added.
kernel_track.mechanism: The standard tree reduction reads/writes sm.red[tid] and sm.red[tid+stride]; at stride 128 the two land on conflicting banks. Padding to 257 (odd) breaks the power-of-2 stride alias. The reduction arithmetic and ascending order are unchanged => bit-identical fp64 result. RISK: must confirm the struct still fits the smem budget and that sm.red isn't aliased/overlaid with another buffer at a fixed offset (it is the engine's shared reduction slot — verify no union/overlay assumes 256). Parity gate covers correctness.
kernel_track.expected_effect: 1-3% per block-reduce latency on grok-enabled cells (GrokAdamW/NeuralGrok/LookSAM/SG11/SG15/SG2); ~0.2-0.5% wall on those runs. AdamW/Lion/Grokfast/Muon/Prodigy mostly unaffected.
kernel_track.synth_note: MERGED mbtc-reduce-smem-bank-conflict + looksam-norm-reduce-opt (the shfl-tree variant) — keep the padding approach (simpler, no barrier-structure change; the shfl variant is risk:med and saves no smem). Must verify smem-arena offset/overlay assumptions before keeping. Real win only on grok cells.

kernel_track.description: Remove the two clamp guards on eidx that can never trigger (ta_i/tb_i come from the top-k insertion sort and are provably in [0,pkd), so eidx in [0,pkd^2)=[0,num_experts)).
kernel_track.mechanism: The expert index is constructed from top-k-selected indices that are bounded by construction, so eidx is always in range and the clamps are dead. Removing them changes no value ever taken (parity-neutral), saving 2 instructions per expert route. RISK: this is the SG2 meta-optimizer (drives all grok cells); the safety guard's removal is only sound if the in-range invariant truly always holds — keep the clamp behavior identical by first adding a debug assert, validate, then drop. Parity gate confirms no behavioral change.
kernel_track.synth_note: Verified the guards exist and are dead under the documented invariant. Tiny ceiling; value is mostly that it's parity-clean and removes branches. Ordered late. Keep only if it shows ANY 3-seed improvement (likely neutral).

PARITY/PERF RISK: reorders commit_group/wait_group relative to the k-loop in wgmma_mainloop_kchain (risk:med). The kchain ordering (one fence, ascending-k issue, commit+wait at end) is the silicon-validated determinism contract; reordering risks the bitwise-reproducible accumulation guarantee. Not clearly neutral.

PARITY RISK on a validated barrier contract: dropping the wgmma_fence before the first issue depends on a caller-side pre-zero/pre-fence guarantee; the megakernels' fresh-tile path relies on the default fence. Mis-applying silently corrupts the first k-step accumulator. Ceiling ~0.5%; not worth the parity exposure.

PARITY RISK (auditor-flagged needs_fp64_parity_gate, risk:med): restructures PEER per-head computation from per-thread to CTA-cooperative with smem head-aggregation. This is the SG2 meta-optimizer feeding all grok cells; moving the head reduction into smem is a non-trivial algorithm refactor that needs a new parity derivation. Violates hard rule (1) 'no rewrites needing new parity derivation'.

PARITY RISK: 2-way unroll of the outer s-loop processing s=i and s=i+2 'independently before converging' changes the insertion order on score ties. sg2_stage_topk is documented to match csa_indexer_topk_kernel exactly with ascending-s tie-break; reordering breaks the stable tie-break and diverges from the fp64 mirror.

PARITY RISK: reorders the GRU h_new = (1-z)*h_old + z*h_tilde arithmetic / early-materializes (1-z)*h_old. The file's own comments (lines 832-839) stress this stage must match the fp64 reference's exact FMA precision; any reassociation can diverge invisibly until the 1e-5 GPU parity gate. Not clearly bit-neutral.

PARITY RISK: 2-4x unroll of the GRU output loop to overlap tanhf latencies across channels. The per-channel reductions (ah += Wh*xin) are independent so order is fine, BUT this is on the precision-sensitive GRU path; combined with the explicit accurate-transcendental discipline (expf/tanhf must match torch), an aggressive unroll that lets the compiler reassociate the k-reduction risks a parity drift. Excluded under the conservative neutral-only rule.

PARITY RISK (low but nonzero): 2-way unroll + pipelining of the expert MLP ReLU chain (W1*g+b1 -> relu -> W2*relu) on the SG2 meta-optimizer path. Reordering FMAs across the ReLU on the all-grok-cells critical numeric path is not guaranteed bit-identical; ceiling ~1-2% of PEER doesn't justify the parity exposure.

PARITY-ADJACENT RISK / heavy refactor: moves the top-k insertion-sort state from per-thread registers to a CTA-synchronous smem buffer, introducing a new sync phase into topk. risk:med; changes the topk dataflow structure on the meta-optimizer path. Too invasive for the neutral-only ratchet; needs its own derivation/validation.

EXPLICITLY NON-NEUTRAL: auditor states 'unpredictable; could be +5% (worse) or -5% (better)', needs_fp64_parity_gate, confidence low. Adding a maxreg cap to sg2_meta_optimizer_megakernel is a speculative occupancy gamble, directly violating the neutral-or-positive hard rule.

MICRO (<0.1%, one arithmetic op/trial) and confidence med. Real but immeasurably small; below the noise floor of 3-seed timing. Not worth a ratchet slot.

MERGED into version-gated-flags-cache (pre-warm vs lazy-cache the same probe; auditor itself says 'Negligible per-build, probe already cached'). Subsumed.

Suppressing them would blind the very gate doing the judging. Keep diagnostics ON during the campaign.

summary: The highest-value, lowest-risk wins are all host-side or search-machinery hoists that are bit-neutral by construction: in compile.py, drop JSON indent on cache saves, cache the per-arch nvcc version/flags probe, hoist the per-trial build-signature hash and loop-invariant featurize/seed-trial/early-stop computations out of hot loops, and swap the measured-ms rolling window to a deque — these bank fast because the in-file _self_test gate plus build/tune time judge them and none touch emitted kernel semantics. On the kernel side the safest ratchet leader is caching n_sms in the launcher scratch (pure host-side, parity-trivial), followed by a small family of order-preserving #pragma-unroll bumps on fixed-bound fp32 loops (vit head-logits 4->8, vit attn-bwd kSeq=17, mamba staging) that keep accumulation order identical, plus one real smem bank-conflict fix (pad sm.red to 257 floats) that helps only the grok-enabled cells. The single biggest synthesis finding is that an entire cluster of tile_pipeline.cuh candidates (descriptor_cache_reuse, producer_btree_reduction, consume_loop_async_interleave, cp_async_batch_prefetch, producer_slot_early_compute, parity/alignment init) target tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16 / pipeline_produce_ktile / TilePipeline, which grep confirms are SELF-TEST-ONLY and never called by any production megakernel — they would pass the parity gate yet move zero production step-time, so they are dropped as production dead-code; the real production GEMM staging is tc_gemm_block_unpipelined's already-KEPT cp.async ring. Most SuperGrok2 candidates were dropped either as already-satisfied no-ops (every stage pointer already carries __restrict__) or as parity risks on the meta-optimizer's precision-sensitive GRU/top-k/expert paths (insertion-sort tie-break reorders, GRU FMA reassociation, maxreg gambles), and three compile candidates (prefilter-env-dict-reuse, descriptor_base_offset_constexpr-as-already-folded, dec-ln-fwd-const-ptr) were confirmed already implemented in the source.
